literal: Large it is, sharp-tusked it is, even if, the elephant will fear, tiger if attacks.
translation: Even if an elephant is massive and armed with sharp tusks, it will shrink in fear if a tiger attacks.
modern: யானை உருவத்தில் பெரியதாகவும் கூர்மையான தந்தங்களை உடையதாகவும் இருந்தாலும், ஒரு புலி தாக்கினால் அது பயந்து நடுங்கும்.
explanation: The couplet contrasts the massive, well-armed elephant with the smaller but fiercely energetic tiger. Even though the elephant possesses a huge body and sharp tusks, it will flee in terror when attacked by a tiger. The tiger represents unyielding enthusiasm and courage, while the elephant represents mere physical strength without the driving force of inner energy. This illustrates that true strength lies in one's spirit and energy, not just in physical size or outward advantages.
